entities.summary:
Story of Sinuhe

Ancient Egyptian literary work

Created around 1874 BCE by an anonymous author

The story of Sinuhe is one of the oldest surviving works of literature from ancient Egypt, predating the Pyramid Texts and the Epic of Gilgamesh.

It tells the tale of Sinuhe, a trusted advisor to Pharaoh Amenemhat III, who flees Egypt after discovering a plot to assassinate the pharaoh. Sinuhe embarks on a perilous journey, encountering various cultures and meeting famous figures such as the Phoenician king Hiram and the biblical figure of the prophet Elisha.

The story is significant not only for its unique blend of Egyptian, Phoenician, and Mesopotamian influences but also for its exploration of themes such as identity, loyalty, and the complexities of human relationships.

Through its use of symbolism, mythology, and philosophical introspection, the Story of Sinuhe offers a nuanced portrayal of the human condition, one that continues to resonate with readers today.

In the 19th century, European scholars such as Auguste Sayce and Gustave Flaubert popularized the text, and it has since been translated into numerous languages, cementing its place as a cornerstone of world literature.
